name: Southwest Face
descent_text: From the summit, downclimb a short way down the north side, then work west to a rappel anchor. A single-rope rappel to the west lands on the Marble Creek glacier; downclimbing to the east has been tried and does not go. Contour east on the glacier to a saddle, rappel a loose gully, cross the moat at the bottom, and descend an unnamed glacier to rejoin the approach. Retrace the approach back through Dorado Col, and expect loose rock in the gully and an awkward moat.
approach: Two approaches are in use. One climbs from the Eldorado trailhead to the base of Eldorado's East Ridge, crosses the Inspiration and McAllister glaciers (obvious crevasses that are easy to avoid) and reaches Dorado Col. The alternative goes by Sibley Pass and Triad Col. From Dorado Col, drop into the Marble Creek cirque over bare ice and snow to roughly 6,000 ft, contour west along a bench, then climb a snow gully to the foot of the southwest face. Good bivy sites are at the base of Eldorado's East Ridge, at Dorado Col, and on the 6,000 ft bench in the cirque.
overview: The Southwest Face holds an adventurous line on rock that is surprisingly good for the area. It uses the main crack system dividing the face, then angles right to the ridge crest once the face steepens. The face climbing runs mostly in the middle of 5th class, with some harder moves, and a roof crux at 5.9 (wet). On the ridge crest it gets easier, but the rock turns much worse.
fa: Richard Emerson, Tom Hornbein, 1971 (to headwall base); Gary Brill, Lowell Skoog, Mark Bebie, 1981 (ridge variation)
